_comment: Copy this file to config.json (the setup wizard does it for you). DO NOT commit config.json - it contains your GitHub token.
_signing_comment: Optional anti-spoofing. Run `python generate_keys.py`, put the PRIVATE key here and the PUBLIC key in the app. Leave empty to publish unsigned (current behaviour).
_interval_comment: How often a full collect/test/publish cycle starts, so dead servers drop and new ones appear. 5 = every 5 min. Cycles never overlap: if one runs longer than this (likely at 10k configs with tcp_prefilter off), the next just starts right after it finishes.
_dashboard_comment: Local web console (logs, server table, delete, update). install.sh fills in a random dashboard_token. Open http://SERVER_IP:8787/?token=THE_TOKEN. Empty token = no auth (only behind a firewall/SSH tunnel).

test._tcp_prefilter_comment: OFF: a raw TCP connect from Iran falsely drops many working CDN/domain-fronted configs (they only work through xray with proper SNI/routing). Skipping it tests everything via xray -> more real servers, at the cost of a slower cycle.
test._concurrency_comment: Testing runs in two passes. SCREENING is wide and shallow: one probe per endpoint, no extras, screen_concurrency at a time. Almost every endpoint in the pool is dead or blocked from Iran, and proving that is a socket on a timeout rather than CPU, so running many at once is nearly free. Measured on the 2-core box: the same fixed sample screened at 16, 48 and 128 at once returned exactly the same endpoints, and only the speed changed - so this number costs nothing but time. MEASURING then runs only over what answered, measure_concurrency at a time, and that number must stay LOW or every ping is really a measure of our own load. parallel_batches is the number of xray processes allowed to exist at once, each holding batch_size SOCKS inbounds; raise batch_size before parallel_batches, since each process costs a startup the whole batch waits through.
test._publish_comment: Only servers whose real measured delay is <= publish_max_ping (ms) are published to the gist. Keeps the app's list genuinely fast. max_ping is the looser test-time cutoff (kept a little above publish_max_ping so a borderline server's warm sample can still qualify); publish_max_ping is the strict publish cutoff that actually decides what ships.
test._accuracy_comment: measure_concurrency caps how many probes run at once in the MEASURING pass, and it is what keeps pings honest: too high and every probe queues behind the others, so a 100ms server reads as 2000ms. 12-24 on a small VPS. Each survivor gets one unmeasured warm-up request first (a fresh tunnel pays for the TCP connect and the TLS handshake, which is not what we want to publish) and then ping_samples measured ones, keeping the fastest.
test._censored_comment: THE important check. test_url is a Google 204, and Google is not blocked here — fine for latency, useless as proof that a config gets past the filter: one whose outbound quietly degrades to direct passes it and gets published. Every survivor is now also asked for a destination this network BLOCKS, through the same tunnel; only a real tunnel can answer. Several targets, first one to answer wins. Set require_censored false to go back to the old behaviour.
test._throughput_comment: A node that handshakes and then trickles is alive and useless. min_kbps > 0 downloads throughput_bytes through each surviving tunnel and drops anything slower. OFF by default because it costs real bandwidth on this VPS: throughput_bytes per survivor, every cycle (300 survivors x 64 KB x 12 cycles/hour is about 230 MB/hour). 50-100 is a sane value if you turn it on.
test._reliability_comment: One cycle is a snapshot, and free nodes are not stable at that timescale: one that passes now and dies in four minutes still reaches a user as a working server. Each endpoint keeps the outcome of its last reliability_window cycles in state/reliability.json; anything below min_reliability is not published, and the list is ordered by that score before latency. A node is never judged on its score until it has reliability_min_samples cycles of history, so newly found servers are never locked out. min_reliability 0 disables the filter (the score is still recorded and still sorts).
test._geo_comment: geo_via_tunnel asks Cloudflare's trace endpoint THROUGH each tunnel to learn the real exit IP + country, so CDN-fronted/chained configs get the correct flag (not the misleading address-based country). Turn off only if it slows the cycle too much.

_sources_comment: Chosen on measured contribution, not on how many links a file advertises: these repos copy from each other, so several of the biggest add nothing the pool already has. Audited from the server (12133 unique endpoints across this list); anything whose every endpoint was already covered by another source was dropped. Every cycle logs `source yield: N alive / M tested` per source, which is the number to add or drop one on. Unchanged files cost nothing to re-check - the fetcher is conditional (ETag/304).
